newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong shippers warn on new airport fees.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong shippers warn on new airport fees.

text.p: The chairman of the Hong Kong Shippers' Council, Chan Wing Kee, has warned that Hong Kong is liable to price itself out of the market if charges at Chek Lap Kok airport are not kept within users' ability to pay.

Writing in the latest edition of the council's magazine, Shippers Today, Chan said because of the detrimental effect excessive charges at the new airport would have on Hong Kong's economy, there is a case for the Government to consider cross-subdidisation.
Chan said one fifth of Hong Kong's external trade by value is by air and air services are playing an increasingly important part in the service economy.
He called for money gained from the redevelopment of prime real estate at Hong Kong's soon to be redundant airport at Kai Tak be partly used to support Chek Lap Kok's opening.
"Its location (Kai Tak) would make it a gold mine for any redevelopment project and any commercial gains to be realised could be used to support CLK's opening," Chan wrote.

He also said a reply is still awaited from the Government on whether it will back a proposal by small freight forwarders and Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals Limited (HACTL) to retain Terminal 2 as a downtown operations centre to consolidate small shipments.

"Given our experience with the saga of terminal handling charges in the seafreight side, shippers do not deserve a copy of this in airfreight operations as well. To strengthen ourselves as a service economy, we must ensure that our services are cost-competitive especially with our neighbours (such as Guangzhou and Shenzhen airports), since they can always beat us at the game," Chan added.

Last week, a seventh round of talks between the Airport Authority and airline representatives ended without airlines knowing how much they will have to pay to use Chek Lap Kok due to open next April. Another round of talks will be held in October.

Freight forwarders are also waiting for HACTL to publish a list of charges for cargo handling at its Superterminal One complex now under construction at Chek Lap Kok. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
